steps.analyst_reply: {"root_cause": "The model has only the holistic choice feature, so with a heavily attorney-skewed training fit it predicts attorney even when the text explicitly states the person is a paralegal (paralegal certificate, 'practicing as a paralegal since 2006', 'senior paralegal') -- a single soft holistic score cannot overcome the prior. Conversely, the forced-choice holistic leans paralegal on texts with no legal content at all (fiction writer, journalist, film plot, counselor), producing false-paralegal errors on items the base rate says are attorney. The scorecard is missing explicit credential/role signals and a detector for whether the text is even about legal work.", "add_elements": [{"key": "states_paralegal_role", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text explicitly describe this person as a paralegal or legal assistant, or mention them earning a paralegal certificate, diploma, or completing a paralegal program?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "licensed_to_practice_law", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text say this person is licensed to practice law, has been admitted to a bar, or currently works as an attorney, lawyer, barrister, or solicitor?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "about_legal_work", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this text mainly about this person's work, career, or studies in the legal field, such as a law firm, court, legal practice, or legal education?", "criteria": null}], "retire_elements": [], "reword_elements": []}
